openai/gpt-5.6-sol.title: MAX_PAYLOAD is 65536, admitting a payload one byte above the 65535-byte contract limit.
CRC-16-CCITT starts at 0x0000 instead of the required 0xFFFF, breaking wire interoperability.
The backpressure length addition is unchecked and can overflow before comparison with HIGH_WATER.
The public consume method accepts values larger than the available data and can overflow or corrupt the read cursor.
Feeding after partial consumption never reclaims the consumed prefix, allowing physical buffer storage to grow without bound.
The parser slices the declared payload and trailer without first checking that the complete frame is buffered.
A checksum failure consumes the entire declared frame instead of resynchronizing at the next magic sequence.
A checksum mismatch is silently reported as an incomplete frame instead of returning FrameError.
Drain discards every parsing error, preventing malformed frames from surfacing to its caller.
Resynchronization discards a trailing first magic byte, breaking magic sequences split across feed boundaries.

fireworks-ai/accounts/fireworks/models/g.title: CRC-16 initial value is 0x0000 but INTENT P1 requires 0xFFFF, so every checksum is computed with the wrong parameterization and frames are non-interoperable with conformant peers (K3).
MAX_PAYLOAD is 65536 but INTENT P2 caps payload length at 65535, so encode accepts a 65536-byte payload and parse accepts len=65536, both one byte over the contract.

next_frame slices data[HEADER_LEN..HEADER_LEN+len] and reads the trailer without first checking data.len() >= frame_len, panicking on any partial frame; P2 requires validating the length against buffered data before any slicing.

Checksum mismatch returns Ok(None) instead of Err(FrameError::Corrupt), silently dropping the corrupt frame and making the caller see a corrupt frame as 'need more bytes', violating P4's requirement to surface FrameError.
drain discards every FrameError via Err(_) => continue, never surfacing corrupt-frame errors to the caller and silently dropping malformed input in violation of P4.

drain's budget -= consumed is unchecked usize subtraction that underflows when a reentrant handler (K2) feeds bytes producing a frame larger than the remaining budget, panicking in debug builds and wrapping in release.
On checksum failure the parser consumes frame_len, trusting the possibly-corrupt length field, instead of rescanning for the next magic sequence as P4 requires for both magic and checksum failures.
